My parents left me, my sister, and my brother alone in the house. My sister is 18, I'm 17, and my brother is 12. My parents made my sister "in charge" while they were away. I guess that means she's supposed to take care of us and make sure everything is okay. On Sunday, I wanted to go out with my girlfriend for dinner. My sister told me I couldn't leave. When I asked why, she said, "Because I said so." At first, I thought she was joking, but she wasn't. I told her she can boss around my little brother but not me, and I went out with my girlfriend anyway. When I came home, my younger brother had called our mom and told her we were "fighting." My mom called me and said I'm grounded and have to do whatever my sister says because she's "in charge." I tried to protest, but my mom wasn't having it, and I got grounded for disobeying my sister who's acting like a pseudo-parent while they're away. I'm wondering if I did the right thing by going out with my girlfriend despite my sister's orders. Is it AITA (Ask if I'm the Asshole) here? Did I make a mistake by not respecting my sister's authority, or was it okay because she's not really a parent? First, I need to consider the roles here. My sister is 18, and I'm 17. She's older, but she's not a parent. My parents left her in charge, but does that mean she has the same authority as a parent? I don't think so. She's just another teenager, albeit older. So, when she told me I couldn't go out, was I obligated to listen? On one hand, respecting the person in charge makes sense, especially when parents are away. It helps maintain order and ensures everyone's safety. On the other hand, my sister is not a parent, and her authority is limited. She can't make rules that are unreasonable or against what my parents would have allowed. In this case, going out with my girlfriend for dinner doesn't seem like a major issue. It's a normal activity for a 17-year-old. My sister's reaction of saying "Because I said so" seems a bit arbitrary and maybe a bit of a power trip. She's letting the power go to her head, as I thought earlier. When I told her she can boss my little brother but not me, I was asserting my independence. I think that's reasonable because she's not my parent. However, by going out despite her orders, I might have disregarded the structure my parents tried to establish by making her in charge. But then, my mom grounded me for not obeying my sister. Is that fair? My mom is the one who set up the situation by making my sister in charge. If my sister is overstepping her bounds, should I have to suffer the consequences? Or should my sister be held accountable for her actions? Also, my younger brother told my mom about the "fight," which led to me getting grounded. I forgave him because he's just a kid and probably scared. But does that mean I should have handled the situation differently to prevent him from getting involved? I'm also thinking about the bigger picture. How does this situation affect our relationships? If I keep asserting my independence, will it cause more conflicts with my sister? Or is it better to respect her authority to keep the peace? Another angle is the concept of authority and responsibility. My sister was given responsibility, but does that automatically grant her the authority to make decisions about my personal life? Or should there be clear boundaries set by my parents about what she can and cannot decide? In the end, I'm torn between respecting the structure my parents set up and asserting my independence as a nearly adult. I want to make decisions for myself, but I also don't want to cause unnecessary conflict or get into trouble with my parents. Maybe the best approach is to communicate openly with my sister and my parents about the expectations when they're away. Setting clear boundaries and understanding each other's roles could prevent future conflicts. But in this specific instance, I'm still unsure if I did the right thing by going out with my girlfriend despite my sister's orders.
